paragraphs.source_en: There are no downsides to using vision questions because of the positive tone and upbeat message they present. On a typical day, most of the working population remains locked in the present and does not think about the future and what it might bring for them. If you can use vision questions to lift your customers out of the present and into a sunny future, they will be forever grateful to you, not to mention the fact that they will almost certainly want to do business with you.

units.source_en: Getting Past ‘‘What If?’’
Objections and Stalls

paragraphs.source_en: *NOT ALL SALES INTERACTIONS* run smoothly, and sometimes as salespeople we hit a bump in the road. These bumps may be because of our own mishandling of a situation, or they may arise because of a customer’s conflicted feelings about a sale. Either way, if we want to salvage our hard work and make sure that the sale goes through, we need to learn to deal with these obstacles so that the customer’s needs are met.

units.source_en: *The Mistakes Salespeople Make*

paragraphs.source_en: There are six common mistakes that salespeople make when they encounter a customer’s objection or stalling tactic: 109

units.source_en: There are six common mistakes that salespeople make when they encounter a customer’s objection or stalling tactic: 109

paragraphs.source_en: 1\. *Fearing the customer’s reaction.* Many salespeople are afraid of what a customer might say and they end up losing a sales opportunity because they do not discover what the customer really wants. For example, a salesperson dreads hearing the words, ‘‘Your price is too high.’’ It’s almost a knee-jerk reaction to respond with a lower price. Instead, a salesperson should be proactive and try to uncover the unique buying criteria important to the customer so the price objection would never come up in the first place.
